clue.text: Knock-about battle he'd had with Penny-that was the end of it!

definitions.text: that was the end of it!

indicators.note: a knock-about fight is rough and disorderly, so the letters of the following words are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rough brawl with someone called Penny is described, and the speaker declares that settled matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock-about' rearranges BATTLE HED HAD plus PENNY, seventeen letters in all; 'with' just joins the two parts of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom saying events concluded abruptly, as when music strikes up to close a scene.

clue.text: Being almost merciful

indicators.note: almost means the synonym stops one letter short of its full length

parts.note: a merciful person is humane, showing kindness

explanation.surface: Someone is described as nearly showing mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb but is the noun: a creature, a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is a living creature, and a person is the commonest such creature meant.

clue.text: Ran Ivan over? Perfect bliss hereafter for him

indicators.note: over in the sense of knocked over or upset, so the letters of the two names are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A question asks whether someone ran a man named Ivan down, then talks of paradise awaiting him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' rearranges RANIVAN; 'for him' tags on to suggest the victim's afterlife.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the final state of release from suffering, a perfect peace beyond rebirth.

clue.text: Short stroke making Lee-Enfield double-barrelled

parts.note: a double-barrelled name such as Lee-Enfield is joined by a short dash between its two parts; the rifle imagery misleads

explanation.surface: A gunsmith's note on converting a Lee-Enfield rifle into a twin-barrelled weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lee-Enfield was a British army rifle, but here the name just stands for any double-barrelled (two-part) name.
explanation.definitionFit: The short dash links the two halves of a compound word or surname.

clue.text: Graduate discovered quartz in church

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
quartz is a crystalline form of silica, silicon dioxide

explanation.surface: A university graduate finds a vein of quartz inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is an oblong church of Roman design, a title given to some important Catholic churches.

clue.text: Not an employer's failure to exercise a right

parts.note: non is the Latin and prefix form of not
an employer in the sense of one who employs, i.e. uses, something: a user

explanation.surface: An employer is said not to have neglected his legal rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employer' means one who uses a thing, not a boss; non-user is a legal term for not exercising a right, which may lapse.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, non-user is the neglect to use a right or privilege, through which it may be lost.

clue.text: Sharp comment

parts.note: a sharp comment is a cutting or barbed observation, and the phrase plays on sharpness as having a point

explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark aimed at someone is one with a figurative point, as a sharp blade has.

clue.text: Lots moved about lazily in an unemotional way

indicators.note: moved about means the letters of the preceding word are shifted around into a new order

parts.note: doing something lazily is doing it idly

explanation.surface: Lots of people drift about lazily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved about' acts only on the first word; 'lazily' supplies its synonym unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive and showing little feeling, so this adverb describes acting without visible emotion.

clue.text: Make empty remarks disputin' a tile having been removed

indicators.note: having been removed suggests the letters are shifted from their places and set down in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains of trite talk while arguing over a tile that has been taken off a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been removed' rearranges DISPUTINATILE, thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter platitudes is to make trite, hollow remarks, so the verb means talking in empty clichés.

clue.text: Shell of gold by French sea

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A golden shell lies beside the French seashore.
explanation.walkthrough: An ormer is an abalone, a shellfish of the Channel Islands, eaten especially in Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an edible sea mollusc with an ear-shaped shell, also called abalone.

clue.text: Pants a lot suffering after giving birth

indicators.note: suffering in the sense of being hurt or damaged, so the letters of the phrase are distorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman pants heavily, in pain, after having a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Postnatal describes the period immediately following childbirth.

clue.text: Peerless example of an apple

definitions.meaning: an old variety of eating apple carries this name

explanation.definitionFit: The word means having no equal, and is also a name for an old dessert apple variety (and a sweet).

clue.text: Divorce town in Southern Europe

definitions.meaning: a divorce is a separation or break-up of a married couple
a port city on the Dalmatian coast of Croatia

explanation.surface: A couple divorce in a southern European town.
explanation.definitionFit: A marital break-up is a separation, and the same word is a Croatian port on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Catch ten members taking the blame

annotationWithheld.why: Catch ten members taking the blame (6): the parse ENT + RAP needs 'ten' to give ENT, but no clue word signals an anagram and 'members' gives nothing; likely an OCR misreading of the clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Catch ten members taking the blame

clue.text: Officer upset employees

parts.note: to upset a container is to tip it over
the employees of a firm are its staff

explanation.surface: A manager has upset the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is a court officer or sheriff's officer, named from the metal-tipped staff once carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court official who keeps order and makes arrests, an officer of the law.

clue.text: We hear Bill read it and could accept it as true

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: ACC, short for account, is a bill; followed by 'read it' said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone says that once Bill had read it he could believe it.
explanation.walkthrough: ACC is the abbreviation for account, a bill; ACC plus 'read it' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To accredit a statement is to believe or credit it, taking it as true.

clue.text: Glittering decoration required for date with man I arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the words are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A sparkly ornament is needed for a date with a man that I set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges DATE, MAN and I; 'required for' and 'with' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamanté is fabric or trimming set with sparkling artificial gems, a showy ornament.

clue.text: State of the nation

parts.note: read as a kind of state that a nation may be, governed without a monarch, rather than as its condition

explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a sovereign state ruled by elected representatives with no hereditary monarch.

clue.text: Man to remember trams, only some of them

indicators.note: only some of them means only part of the letters of the words are used, a run tucked inside

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a few of the old trams.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across rememBER TRAMs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertram is a man's given name.

clue.text: See 1
Alison and I could make the connection

indicators.note: could make means the letters of the names can be formed into something new by rearranging

explanation.surface: Two people say that together they could link up.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a link or working relationship between parties.

clue.text: Make up two thirds of the list

indicators.note: two thirds of means a nine-letter synonym loses its last three letters

parts.note: an inventory is a detailed list of items

explanation.surface: Someone fabricates two thirds of a list.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent a story is to fabricate it, devising something untrue.

clue.text: Car test or the vehicle undergoing it

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for cars in Britain, set by the old Ministry of Transport

explanation.surface: A clue about a car's test, or the vehicle being tested.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly compulsory roadworthiness check for vehicles over three years old.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a motor in British usage, and it is the vehicle that sits the test.

clue.text: One with a brown cap in an American city?

parts.note: one, a person, is a man
a cap is a hat
tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a brown cap is spotted in a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces join in a different order from the clue, which puts the colour before the headgear; read 'One with a brown cap' as a picture of a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan is the central borough of New York City, often used for the city itself.

clue.text: Something hooked-about a pound in weight

indicators.note: in means the short pieces sit within the weight word

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Something curved weighs roughly a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a bird of prey's curved claw.

clue.text: Book obtained for a new employee

definitions.meaning: a work consulted for information, such as a dictionary or encyclopedia
a testimonial from a previous employer, sought when hiring someone

explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary is a reference book, and a testimonial for a job applicant is also called a reference.

clue.text: Auctions drink on board

indicators.note: on as in on board ship, so the drink is placed within the ship's letters

parts.note: board suggests a ship, SS being the abbreviation for steamship
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: Auctions are held where drinks are served aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a crossword convention for going inside the two-letter steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Auctions are public sales where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Being rude I am short and to the point

parts.note: I am in short form is the contraction I'm
pertinent means relevant, to the point

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to brevity and directness, which come across as rudeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' signals the contracted I'M; 'and' joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Impertinent means insolent and disrespectful, behaving rudely.
